rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom = default delivery; body teaches work, trainer manages room.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -n "discuss\|share with\|tell the room\|neighbor\|neighbour\|pair" run-the-first-experiment.md returned no matches above the maintainer fence (line 81). rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-phase failure mode + escape hatch (story judge blocks ship without both).
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -n "Per-phase failure mode" run-the-first-experiment.md -> line 144, table follows (lines 146-154) with one row per forcing-function phase (Connections, Phase 2 over-fill, Phase 2 gap-deferred, Phase 3 settle, Send-off SHA-pin, Send-off pre-empt, Send-off anxiety), each row naming both a dominant failure mode and a named trainer escape-hatch line.

Strategy doc content-strategy-agentic-engineering-101.md line 384: 'Mood: curious readiness — "I've built enough to try something; let's see what the agent does with it." Stakes back in the room; no compliance framing.' Trace mood_score = 8/10 at the single phase and at close (curriculum/evals/sim-cache/ae101--module--run-the-first-experiment.persona.json). Body honours it: opens on prep-not-completion (Big Idea, lines 3-4), 'Your call' (lines 12, 67) keeps stakes without compliance pressure, and Key Concepts (line 56) frames a stopped run as reading, not failing.

M4's mood is curious readiness, not unease, so the rule's literal not-knowing-vs-having-done-wrong contrast doesn't have an unease beat to test against here; the underlying spirit (uncertainty framed as discovery, not shame) still holds throughout — 'the run is how you find out what's missing' (line 4) and 'Traces are data. Stopping a run that has gone off the rails is reading, not failing' (line 56) both frame not-knowing-yet as the point, never as a student failing to have prepared enough.
